*.text:
(* number ...)
Multiply the arguments; no arguments gives 1.

+.text:
(+ number ...)
adds numbers. No arguments gives 0.

-.text:
(- number ...)
Subtract subsequent arguments from the first; one argument negates.

/.text:
(/ number ...)
Divide left to right; one argument takes the reciprocal. Exact integer divisions stay integers; others produce floats. Zero divisors raise an error.

<.text:
(< number number ...)
Test whether adjacent numbers are strictly increasing. Requires at least two arguments; integers and floats can be mixed.

<=.text:
(<= number number ...)
Test whether adjacent numbers are nondecreasing. Requires at least two arguments; integers and floats can be mixed.

=.text:
(= number ...)
Test whether adjacent numbers are equal. Zero or one argument gives #t; integers and floats can be mixed.

>.text:
(> number number ...)
Test whether adjacent numbers are strictly decreasing. Requires at least two arguments; integers and floats can be mixed.

>=.text:
(>= number number ...)
Test whether adjacent numbers are nonincreasing. Requires at least two arguments; integers and floats can be mixed.

acos.text:
(acos number)
Compute inverse cosine in radians.

and.text:
(and expression ...)
Evaluate left to right until a falsy result; return the last result, or #t with no arguments.

append.text:
(append list ...)
Concatenate proper lists into a list. Dotted tails are rejected.

apply.text:
(apply procedure argument ... sequence)
Call procedure with the leading arguments followed by the elements of a proper list or array; nil contributes no arguments.

array.text:
(array value ...)
Construct a mutable array. [a b c] is array literal syntax.

array?.text:
(array? value)
Return #t when value is an array, otherwise #f.

asin.text:
(asin number)
Compute inverse sine in radians.

atan.text:
(atan y [x])
Return arctangent in radians; two arguments use the quadrant-aware angle of y/x.

begin.text:
(begin expression ...)
Evaluate expressions in order and return the last result, or nil for no expressions.

boolean?.text:
(boolean? value)
Return #t when value is #t or #f, otherwise #f.

buffer.text:
(buffer [value])
Create a mutable string builder, optionally initialized from the value's display representation.

buffer->string.text:
(buffer->string buffer)
Return a string snapshot; the buffer remains available for further appends.

buffer-push!.text:
(buffer-push! buffer value ...)
Append display representations to the buffer and return it.

buffer?.text:
(buffer? value)
Return #t when value is a mutable string buffer, otherwise #f.

car.text:
(car pair)
Return the head of a pair. Passing an empty list or another type raises an error.

cdr.text:
(cdr pair)
Return the tail of a pair. Passing an empty list or another type raises an error.

ceiling.text:
(ceiling number)
Round up to an integer.

compute-restarts.text:
(compute-restarts)
Return an array of active restarts, innermost first.

cond.text:
(cond (test expression ...) ... (else expression ...))
Evaluate the first matching clause. else is the final fallback clause.

condition-of-type?.text:
(condition-of-type? condition type)
Test whether a condition has the named type or a registered subtype.

cons.text:
(cons head tail)
Construct a pair. A proper list ends in () or nil.

copy.text:
(copy collection)
Make a shallow copy of an array, table, or instance; nil returns nil. Instances keep their class, migrate if needed, and share the objects held in their slots.

current-jiffy.text:
(current-jiffy)
Return a monotonic nanosecond counter with an unspecified epoch; subtract readings to measure elapsed time.

current-ns.text:
(current-ns)
Return the current namespace name as a symbol.

current-second.text:
(current-second)
Return wall-clock seconds since the Unix epoch as a float.

def.text:
(def name ["docstring"] value) / (def (name parameter ...) ["docstring"] body ...)
Define or replace a binding. Namespace bindings are live across redefinition. Allowed at top level and in bodies.

def-.text:
(def- name ["docstring"] value) / (def- (name parameter ...) ["docstring"] body ...)
Define or replace a top-level binding that is private to its namespace.

defer.text:
(defer expression cleanup ...)
Run cleanup on normal return and on unwinding. Return expression's value unless cleanup raises a new condition.

define-condition.text:
(define-condition name parent)
Register a condition type and parent for condition-of-type? checks; use nil for no parent.

defmacro.text:
(defmacro name parameters ["docstring"] body ...)
Define an unhygienic Otium macro. It receives unevaluated argument datums and returns replacement code; use gensym for fresh names.

defparam.text:
(defparam name ["docstring"] default)
Define a named dynamically scoped parameter. Call (name) to read it; use with-params to override it temporarily.

describe.text:
(describe 'name)
Return namespace/name: docstring for a binding, a no-documentation placeholder for an undocumented binding, or nil for an unknown name. Runtime forms return their shared reference text.

display.text:
(display value ...)
Write display representations to the current output port sink, separated by spaces, without a newline. Return nil. Writes to current-output-port.

eq?.text:
(eq? a b)
Compare immediate values by value and heap objects by identity. Use equal? for structural comparison.

equal?.text:
(equal? a b)
Compare values structurally, including pairs, arrays, tables, and string contents.

error.text:
(error condition-or-message argument ...)
Raise an error condition containing the message and optional arguments; does not return normally.

eval.text:
(eval form)
Macroexpand and evaluate a datum in the current namespace, without the caller's lexical bindings.

even?.text:
(even? number)
Return #t when the argument is an even integer, otherwise #f.

exact.text:
(exact number)
Convert an integer-valued finite number to an integer; fractional or out-of-range values raise an error.

exact?.text:
(exact? number)
Return #t when the argument is an integer representation, otherwise #f.

exit.text:
(exit [status])
Request program termination with an optional integer exit status from 0 through 255 (default 0).

exp.text:
(exp number)
Compute e raised to the argument as a float.

expander-macro-var.text:
(expander-macro-var symbol)
Internal expander hook: resolve a symbol to its macro value, or nil if it does not name a macro.

expander-invoke-macro.text:
(expander-invoke-macro macro arguments)
Internal expander hook: run a macro's transformer on unevaluated argument forms.

expander-qualify.text:
(expander-qualify symbol)
Internal expander hook: symbol qualified with the namespace that owns it, or with the current namespace when unbound; false to leave it bare.

expander-local-name.text:
(expander-local-name symbol)
Internal expander hook: for a qualified symbol, the bare name when it means the same binding in the current namespace, else false.

expt.text:
(expt base exponent)
Raise base to exponent. Nonnegative integer powers of integers use integer arithmetic with wrapping overflow; other inputs use floating point.

false?.text:
(false? value)
Return #t when value is exactly #f, otherwise #f.

find-restart.text:
(find-restart name)
Find the innermost active restart by name, or return nil.

finite?.text:
(finite? number)
Return #t when the argument is finite, otherwise #f.

float?.text:
(float? value)
Return #t when value is a floating-point representation, otherwise #f.

floor.text:
(floor number)
Round down to an integer.

fn.text:
(fn parameters body ...)
Create a lexical procedure. Parameters may be a proper list, dotted rest list, (a & rest), or a rest symbol.

for-each.text:
(for-each procedure sequence)
Call procedure on each element for side effects, then return nil. Traverses a snapshot; accepts a proper list, array, or nil.

foreign?.text:
(foreign? value)
Return #t when value is a foreign extension value, otherwise #f.

gensym.text:
(gensym [prefix])
Return a fresh symbol using the optional string prefix (default G). Useful for avoiding accidental capture in macros.

get.text:
(get collection key [default])
Look up a table key or an array/string index. Missing entries and nil collections return default (nil if omitted). String indexing returns a char.

handler-bind.text:
(handler-bind ((predicate handler) ...) body ...)
Evaluate all bindings left to right under the surrounding handlers, then install signal-site handlers for body. Returning from a handler declines the condition.

if.text:
(if test consequent [alternative])
Evaluate one branch. Only nil and #f are falsy; omitted alternative returns nil.

inexact.text:
(inexact number)
Convert a number to a float.

inexact?.text:
(inexact? number)
Return #t when the argument is a floating-point representation, otherwise #f.

infinite?.text:
(infinite? number)
Return #t when the argument is positive or negative infinity, otherwise #f.

int?.text:
(int? value)
Return #t when value is an integer representation, otherwise #f.

integer?.text:
(integer? number)
Return #t when the argument is an integer value, including integral floats, otherwise #f.

invoke-restart.text:
(invoke-restart name-or-restart argument ...)
Unwind to the chosen active restart and run its clause with the arguments.

jiffies-per-second.text:
(jiffies-per-second)
Return 1000000000, the number of clock jiffies per second.

keys.text:
(keys table)
Return the table's keys in insertion order as an array. nil gives an empty array. This is a collection operation, not Scheme multiple values.

keyword.text:
(keyword name)
Intern a keyword from a string, symbol, or keyword name.

keyword?.text:
(keyword? value)
Return #t when value is a keyword, otherwise #f.

length.text:
(length collection)
Count list/array elements, table entries, or string/buffer Unicode code points. Improper lists and unsupported types raise an error.

let.text:
(let ((name expression) ...) body ...) / (let loop ((name expression) ...) body ...)
Bind names sequentially: later initializers see earlier bindings. Named let creates a recursive loop.

list.text:
(list value ...)
Construct a proper list of the arguments.

list?.text:
(list? value)
Return #t when value is a proper list (including () and nil-terminated chains), otherwise #f.

log.text:
(log number)
Compute the natural logarithm as a float.

macro?.text:
(macro? value)
Return #t when value is an Otium macro, otherwise #f.

macroexpand.text:
(macroexpand form)
Repeatedly expand head macro calls until the head is no longer a macro. Does not descend into subforms.

macroexpand-all.text:
(macroexpand-all form)
Expand every macro call in form, including subforms, as the evaluator would before compiling it.

macroexpand-1.text:
(macroexpand-1 form)
Expand a macro at the head of form once; otherwise return form unchanged. Does not descend into subforms.

max.text:
(max number ...)
Return the largest of one or more numbers.

min.text:
(min number ...)
Return the smallest of one or more numbers.

modulo.text:
(modulo dividend divisor)
Integer modulus with the divisor's sign. Both arguments must be integers; the divisor must be nonzero.

name.text:
(name value)
Return the name of a symbol or keyword as a string; a string is returned unchanged.

nan?.text:
(nan? number)
Return #t when the argument is not-a-number, otherwise #f.

neg?.text:
(neg? number)
Return #t when the argument is negative, otherwise #f.

newline.text:
(newline [port])
Write a newline to port, defaulting to current-output-port, and return nil.

nil?.text:
(nil? value)
Return #t when value is nil, otherwise #f.

not.text:
(not value)
Return #t for nil or #f; every other value, including (), is truthy.

ns.text:
(ns name [:require clauses])
Select a namespace. Optional (:require ...) clauses import modules; a loaded module must declare its requested name.

null?.text:
(null? value)
Return #t when value is the empty list (), otherwise #f.

number->string.text:
(number->string number)
Return the number's display representation as a string.

number?.text:
(number? value)
Return #t when value is an integer or float, otherwise #f.

odd?.text:
(odd? number)
Return #t when the argument is an odd integer, otherwise #f.

or.text:
(or expression ...)
Evaluate left to right until a truthy result; return the last result, or #f with no arguments.

pair?.text:
(pair? value)
Return #t when value is a pair, otherwise #f.

pop!.text:
(pop! array)
Remove and return the last array element, or nil when empty.

pos?.text:
(pos? number)
Return #t when the argument is positive, otherwise #f.

print.text:
(print value ...)
Write display representations to the current output port sink, separated by spaces, without a newline. Return nil. Writes to current-output-port.

println.text:
(println value ...)
Write display representations to the current output port sink, separated by spaces, followed by a newline. Return nil. Writes to current-output-port.

procedure?.text:
(procedure? value)
Return #t when value is a function or native procedure, otherwise #f.

push!.text:
(push! array value ...)
Append values to the array and return it.

put!.text:
(put! collection key value ...)
Mutate a table or array and return it. Table values of nil delete keys. Array indices must already exist; use push! to grow an array.

quasiquote.text:
(quasiquote template) / `template
Construct data from a template, evaluating active unquote and unquote-splicing forms.

quit.text:
(quit [status])
Request program termination; status defaults to 0 and must be an integer from 0 through 255.

quote.text:
(quote datum) / 'datum
Return datum without evaluating it.

quotient.text:
(quotient dividend divisor)
Integer division truncated toward zero. Both arguments must be integers; the divisor must be nonzero.

read-string.text:
(read-string string)
Read exactly one form without evaluating it. Empty input or trailing forms raise an error.

remainder.text:
(remainder dividend divisor)
Integer remainder with the dividend's sign. Both arguments must be integers; the divisor must be nonzero.

require.text:
(require module [:as alias] [:refer (names)] [:reload])
Load a namespace. Grouped and quoted specs are also accepted. Search each path directory for .ot then .scm. Reload reevaluates the namespace, preserving defonce values and effects before an error.

restart-case.text:
(restart-case expression (name ["description"] parameters body ...) ...)
Make named recovery clauses available during expression and clause evaluation. invoke-restart unwinds to the selected clause; a clause may invoke itself or a sibling restart.

restart-description.text:
(restart-description restart)
Return a restart's description string, or nil if it has none.

restart-name.text:
(restart-name restart)
Return a restart's name as a symbol.

reverse.text:
(reverse sequence)
Reverse a list or array, preserving its kind. nil is treated as an empty list.

round.text:
(round number)
Round to the nearest integer; halfway cases round away from zero.

set!.text:
(set! name value)
Replace the value of an existing lexical or namespace binding.

set-car!.text:
(set-car! pair value)
Replace the pair's head and return the pair. Cycles and mutation of pairs frozen as table keys are rejected.

set-cdr!.text:
(set-cdr! pair value)
Replace the pair's tail and return the pair. Cycles and mutation of pairs frozen as table keys are rejected.

signal.text:
(signal condition-or-message argument ...)
Offer a condition to active handlers before unwinding. Returning from a handler declines; if all decline, return nil.

sqrt.text:
(sqrt number)
Compute the square root as a float.

str.text:
(str value ...)
Concatenate display representations into a string, with no separators. No arguments gives an empty string.

string->number.text:
(string->number string)
Parse an integer or float, allowing surrounding whitespace. Invalid numeric text returns nil.

string->symbol.text:
(string->symbol name)
Intern a symbol from a string, symbol, or keyword name.

string-append.text:
(string-append string ...)
Concatenate strings; non-string arguments raise an error.

string-contains?.text:
(string-contains? string text)
Return #t if string contains the literal text, otherwise #f.

string-downcase.text:
(string-downcase string)
Convert ASCII uppercase letters to lowercase.

string-ends-with?.text:
(string-ends-with? string text)
Return #t if string ends with the literal text, otherwise #f.

string-join.text:
(string-join separator sequence)
Join the display representations of sequence elements with separator.

string-length.text:
(string-length string)
Count Unicode code points, not encoded bytes.

string-replace.text:
(string-replace string from to)
Replace every literal occurrence of from with to.

string-split.text:
(string-split string [separator])
Split into an array on a literal nonempty separator, or on runs of whitespace when omitted.

string-starts-with?.text:
(string-starts-with? string text)
Return #t if string starts with the literal text, otherwise #f.

string-upcase.text:
(string-upcase string)
Convert ASCII lowercase letters to uppercase.

string<?.text:
(string<? left right)
Test lexicographic string ordering.

string?.text:
(string? value)
Return #t when value is a string, otherwise #f.

substring.text:
(substring string start [end])
Copy code points from start (inclusive) to end (exclusive, default length). Indices clamp to the string bounds; end below start gives an empty string.

symbol.text:
(symbol name)
Intern a symbol from a string, symbol, or keyword name.

symbol->string.text:
(symbol->string symbol)
Return the symbol's name as a string.

symbol?.text:
(symbol? value)
Return #t when value is a symbol, otherwise #f.

table.text:
(table key value ...)
Construct an insertion-ordered table. Requires key/value pairs; a nil value removes its key. {key value ...} is table literal syntax.

table?.text:
(table? value)
Return #t when value is a table, otherwise #f.

true?.text:
(true? value)
Return #t when value is exactly #t, otherwise #f.

truncate.text:
(truncate number)
Round toward zero to an integer.

try.text:
(try body ... (catch (predicate name) handler-body ...) ...)
Catch an unwinding condition using the first matching predicate. (catch name body ...) catches any condition. quit is not caught.

type.text:
(type value)
Return the value's type as a keyword, such as :int, :string, :array, or :table.

unquote.text:
(unquote expression) / ,expression
Insert an evaluated value into an enclosing quasiquote.

unquote-splicing.text:
(unquote-splicing expression) / ,@expression
Splice evaluated sequence elements into an enclosing quasiquote.

unwind-protect.text:
(unwind-protect expression cleanup ...)
Run cleanup on normal return and on unwinding. Return expression's value unless cleanup raises a new condition.

update!.text:
(update! collection key procedure argument ...)
Replace the entry with (procedure (get collection key) argument ...). Mutates and returns the collection.

values.text:
(values table)
Return the table's values in insertion order as an array. nil gives an empty array. This is a collection operation, not Scheme multiple values.

while.text:
(while test body ...)
Repeat body while test is truthy, then return nil.

with-params.text:
(with-params ((parameter value) ...) body ...)
Install dynamic parameter values sequentially for body, restoring them on every exit path.

write.text:
(write value ...)
Write readable representations to the current output port sink, separated by spaces, without a newline. Return nil. Writes to current-output-port.

zero?.text:
(zero? number)
Return #t when the argument is zero, otherwise #f.

defonce.text:
(defonce name ["docstring"] expression)
Initialize a binding once, preserving its value and documentation on reload.

reset-generic!.text:
(reset-generic! (name argument ...))
Replace this declaration with a fresh generic of the given arity and no methods.

expander-locate.text:
(expander-locate from to)
Internal shared-expander adapter that carries source positions through expansion.

expander-fail.text:
(expander-fail code message form)
Internal shared-expander adapter that raises a coded syntax error.

read-file.text:
(read-file path)
Read a whole UTF-8 text file into a string; raise an error if it cannot be read.

symbol-macrolet.text:
(symbol-macrolet ((name expansion [(parameter write-form)]) ...) body ...)
Replace references to name with expansion in body. With a writer, (set! name value) becomes (let ((parameter value)) write-form).

remove-method!.text:
(remove-method! generic signature [qualifier])
Remove a method with the given class/#f signature and return whether one existed. Object and #f both mean unspecialized. The qualifier defaults to primary; :around removes a wrapper.

set-applied!.text:
(set-applied! object key value)
Assign an instance slot, table key, or existing array index and return value. (set! (object key) value) evaluates object, key, and value once, in that order. Table values of nil delete keys.

reset-class!.text:
(reset-class! Name [:is Abstract] slot ...)
Explicitly replace an existing local binding with a fresh concrete class. Old instances and signatures retain the old class identity.

generic-methods.text:
(generic-methods generic)
Return detached (qualifier signature) lists. Qualifiers are primary or :around. Signatures contain class descriptors; Object represents an unspecialized argument.

update-instance.text:
(update-instance object old-slots)
Generic called after lazy migration. old-slots is a table of the previous keyword slot values. The default does nothing. Methods may initialize newly required slots; a failed migration is retried on the next access.

slot-set!.text:
(slot-set! instance keyword value)
Write a declared slot and return value. Migrates an outdated instance before writing. Read slots by calling the instance: (instance keyword).

instance?.text:
(instance? value)
Test whether value is a class instance. Instances have identity equality and are not tables.

make.text:
(make Class keyword value ...)
Construct a concrete class instance. Supplied keywords must name declared slots; repeated keywords keep the last value. Missing slots evaluate their defaults in declaration order or raise an error when required.

defabstract.text:
(defabstract Name [:is Parent])
Declare a slotless abstract type for dispatch. Parents must be abstract and acyclic; the default parent is Object. Abstract types cannot be instantiated.

with-slots.text:
(with-slots object (slot ...) body ...)
Evaluate object once and bind local symbol macros that read and write its slots. Each read sees the current value; set! on a slot name writes through to the object.

dispatch-type.text:
(dispatch-type value)
Return the class used for generic dispatch, including the declared class of an instance.

defclass.text:
(defclass Name [:is Abstract] slot ...)
Declare a final class with fixed slots. Slot options are :init expression, :accessor generic, and :state boolean. State slots require :init; ordinary make treats them like other slots. Reload preserves class identity and lazily migrates instances; changing a slot between property and state resets it.

defgeneric.text:
(defgeneric (name argument ...))
Declare a fixed-arity generic. Reload preserves its identity and methods.

defmethod.text:
(defmethod [:around] (generic parameter ...) [:next name] body ...)
Add or replace a method by qualifier and signature. :next binds a lexical procedure for the remaining methods, or #f when none remain. Pass every argument explicitly. Around methods wrap primary methods; incomparable applicable methods are ambiguous.

class-properties.text:
(class-properties Class keyword value ...)
Construct properties for a fresh description. Reject state initargs, evaluate property defaults, and fill state slots with nil without evaluating their initializers. Used by otium.ui.

class-mount.text:
(class-mount properties)
Copy current-layout properties to a new instance and initialize its state slots. Does not repeat property initializers. Rejects stale descriptions after class redefinition.

class-update-properties!.text:
(class-update-properties! instance properties)
Update an instance from current-layout properties of the same class, preserving state slots. During migration, supplies new required properties before update-instance runs. Returns the original instance; a failed migration restores its old layout and slots.

class-subtype?.text:
(class-subtype? child parent)
Test whether child is parent or descends from it through abstract parents. Both arguments must be class descriptors.

char?.text:
(char? value)
Test whether value is a char.

char->integer.text:
(char->integer char)
The Unicode code point of char.

integer->char.text:
(integer->char n)
The char with code point n; raise an error for surrogates and values above #x10FFFF.

char-upcase.text:
(char-upcase char)
Uppercase an ASCII letter; other chars are returned unchanged on C.

char-downcase.text:
(char-downcase char)
Lowercase an ASCII letter; other chars are returned unchanged on C.

char-alphabetic?.text:
(char-alphabetic? char)
Test for a letter. ASCII-only on C.

char-numeric?.text:
(char-numeric? char)
Test for a decimal digit. ASCII-only on C.

char-whitespace?.text:
(char-whitespace? char)
Test for whitespace. ASCII-only on C.

string.text:
(string char ...)
Build a string from chars.

string->list.text:
(string->list string)
A list of the chars in string.

list->string.text:
(list->string list)
Build a string from a list of chars.

string-ref.text:
(string-ref string k)
The char at code point index k; raise an error when out of range. O(k) on C, which stores strings as UTF-8.

eof-object?.text:
(eof-object? value)
Test whether value is the end-of-file object.

bytevector.text:
(bytevector byte ...)
Create a fresh mutable bytevector. Each byte must be an exact integer from 0 to 255.

bytevector?.text:
(bytevector? value)
Test whether value is a bytevector.

make-bytevector.text:
(make-bytevector length [fill])
Create a bytevector of non-negative length, filled with fill (default 0). Fill must be a byte from 0 to 255.

bytevector-length.text:
(bytevector-length bytes)
Return the number of bytes.

bytevector-u8-ref.text:
(bytevector-u8-ref bytes index)
Return the byte at index. Raise an error for an invalid index.

bytevector-u8-set!.text:
(bytevector-u8-set! bytes index byte)
Set the byte at index and return nil. Reject invalid indexes and values outside 0 to 255.

bytevector-copy.text:
(bytevector-copy bytes [start [end]])
Copy the half-open byte range into a fresh bytevector. Defaults to the whole bytevector.

bytevector-copy!.text:
(bytevector-copy! to at from [start [end]])
Copy a half-open range from from into to at byte index at. Overlapping ranges are supported. Return nil.

bytevector-append.text:
(bytevector-append bytes ...)
Concatenate bytevectors into a fresh bytevector.

utf8->string.text:
(utf8->string bytes [start [end]])
Decode a half-open byte range as UTF-8. Invalid input raises decode-error with the absolute byte offset in :position.

string->utf8.text:
(string->utf8 text [start [end]])
Encode a half-open character range as UTF-8 in a fresh bytevector. Defaults to the whole string.

call-with-cleanup.text:
(call-with-cleanup body cleanup)
Call body with no arguments and cleanup with its exit outcome on every exit. The outcome is nil on return or restart transfer, the condition on error, or :quit on exit or interrupt. Cleanup errors replace the pending result. Reentry through a continuation is unsupported.

port?.text:
(port? value)
Test whether value is an Otium port.

input-port?.text:
(input-port? value)
Test whether value is an input port.

output-port?.text:
(output-port? value)
Test whether value is an output port.

input-port-open?.text:
(input-port-open? value)
Test whether value is an open input port.

output-port-open?.text:
(output-port-open? value)
Test whether value is an open output port.

open-input-file.text:
(open-input-file path [options])
Open a buffered byte input port. Options may specify a positive :buffer-size.

open-output-file.text:
(open-output-file path [options])
Open a buffered output port. :if-exists is :truncate (default), :append, or :error. :buffer-size is a positive byte count.

open-input-string.text:
(open-input-string text)
Open a byte input port over the UTF-8 encoding of text.

open-input-bytevector.text:
(open-input-bytevector bytes)
Open an input port over a snapshot of bytes.

open-output-string.text:
(open-output-string)
Create a byte output port whose contents can be decoded with get-output-string.

open-output-bytevector.text:
(open-output-bytevector)
Create an output port collecting bytes.

get-output-string.text:
(get-output-string port)
Return the string port contents without consuming them. Invalid UTF-8 raises decode-error.

get-output-bytevector.text:
(get-output-bytevector port)
Return a fresh bytevector with the output contents, without consuming them.

close-port.text:
(close-port port)
Flush an output port and close the port. Closing twice does nothing.

close-input-port.text:
(close-input-port port)
Close an input port. Closing twice does nothing.

close-output-port.text:
(close-output-port port)
Flush and close an output port. Closing twice does nothing.

read-char.text:
(read-char [port])
Read one Unicode scalar, or the EOF object. Invalid UTF-8 raises decode-error at the byte :position.

peek-char.text:
(peek-char [port])
Decode the next character without consuming any bytes, or return EOF.

read-u8.text:
(read-u8 [port])
Read a byte as an integer, or the EOF object.

peek-u8.text:
(peek-u8 [port])
Return the next byte without consuming it, or EOF.

read-bytevector.text:
(read-bytevector count [port])
Read up to count bytes, stopping at EOF. Return EOF if none are available; count zero returns an empty bytevector.

read-bytevector!.text:
(read-bytevector! bytes [port [start [end]]])
Fill a half-open byte range without allocating a result buffer. Return the byte count, or EOF when no bytes are available.

%read-characters.text:
(%read-characters count [port])
Runtime implementation of the count-based read-string form.

read-all.text:
(read-all [port])
Read the remaining input as UTF-8 text. Return an empty string at EOF.

read.text:
(read [port])
Read one Otium datum, or the EOF object.

read-line.text:
(read-line [port])
Read a line without its newline and preceding carriage return. Preserve a final unterminated line. Return EOF when no text remains.

read-until.text:
(read-until stops [port])
Read characters before the next member of stops, leaving that character unread. Return a string even at EOF.

read-while.text:
(read-while characters [port])
Read the longest prefix drawn from characters. Return a string even at EOF.

skip-while.text:
(skip-while characters [port])
Skip the longest prefix drawn from characters and return its character count.

write-string.text:
(write-string text [port [start [end]]])
Write a half-open character range as UTF-8; indexes cost O(end) on C. Return nil.

write-char.text:
(write-char character [port])
Write one Unicode scalar as UTF-8 and return nil.

write-u8.text:
(write-u8 byte [port])
Write an exact integer byte from 0 to 255 and return nil.

write-bytevector.text:
(write-bytevector bytes [port [start [end]]])
Write a half-open byte range and return nil.

flush-output-port.text:
(flush-output-port [port])
Write buffered bytes to the sink and invoke its flush callback.

make-input-port.text:
(make-input-port name callbacks)
Create a buffered input port. :read receives (bytes start end) and returns a positive count or EOF. :close is optional.

make-output-port.text:
(make-output-port name callbacks)
Create a buffered output port. :write receives (bytes start end) and returns a positive count. :flush and :close are optional.

open-ports.text:
(open-ports)
Return an array of open file, custom, and standard ports; excludes memory ports.

display-to.text:
(display-to port value ...)
Write display forms separated by spaces to port and return nil.

write-to.text:
(write-to port value ...)
Write readable forms separated by spaces to port and return nil.

flush-ports!.text:
(flush-ports!)
Flush all open file and custom output ports and the default output and error ports.

file-exists?.text:
(file-exists? path)
Test whether the path exists. Other filesystem failures raise file-error.

file-symbolic-link?.text:
(file-symbolic-link? path)
Test whether path itself is a symbolic link, including a dangling link.

current-directory.text:
(current-directory)
Return the current working directory as an absolute path.

file-info.text:
(file-info path)
Return a table with :type (:file, :directory, or :other), :size in bytes, and :modified in Unix seconds.

delete-file.text:
(delete-file path)
Delete a file and return nil. Filesystem failures raise file-error.

rename-file.text:
(rename-file from to)
Rename a file and return nil. Filesystem failures raise file-error.

make-directory.text:
(make-directory path)
Create a directory and return nil. Filesystem failures raise file-error.

list-directory.text:
(list-directory path)
Return a sorted array of entry names, excluding . and ... Filesystem failures raise file-error.

current-input-port.text:
(current-input-port)
The dynamically scoped default input port. Rebind with with-params.

current-output-port.text:
(current-output-port)
The dynamically scoped default output port. Rebind with with-params.

current-error-port.text:
(current-error-port)
The dynamically scoped error output port. Rebind with with-params.

open-binary-input-file.text:
(open-binary-input-file path [options])
Alias for open-input-file; all ports support byte and text reads.

open-binary-output-file.text:
(open-binary-output-file path [options])
Alias for open-output-file; all ports support byte and text writes.

bitwise-and.text:
(bitwise-and integer ...)
Bitwise AND of exact integers; no arguments gives -1.

bitwise-ior.text:
(bitwise-ior integer ...)
Bitwise inclusive OR of exact integers; no arguments gives 0.

bitwise-xor.text:
(bitwise-xor integer ...)
Bitwise exclusive OR of exact integers; no arguments gives 0.

bitwise-not.text:
(bitwise-not integer)
Complement the bits of one exact integer.

bitwise-arithmetic-shift.text:
(bitwise-arithmetic-shift integer count)
Shift an exact integer left by count bits, or right with sign extension for a negative count. C raises an error if the result exceeds its integer range.

record-new.text:
(record-new Type value ...)
Construct a record with positional values in declaration order. Every field is required.

record-ref.text:
(record-ref record :field)
Read a record field. Records also support (record :field). Unknown fields are errors.

record-set!.text:
(record-set! record :field value)
Write a mutable record field and return value. Immutable records reject writes; immutability is shallow.

record?.text:
(record? value)
Test whether value is a record instance.

record-type?.text:
(record-type? value)
Test whether value is a record type descriptor.

record-type.text:
(record-type record)
Return the record type descriptor. Records compare by identity, including immutable records.

class?.text:
(class? value)
Test whether value is a class descriptor.

generic?.text:
(generic? value)
Test whether value is a generic function.

type-descriptor?.text:
(type-descriptor? value)
Test whether value is a type descriptor, such as a class.

type-name.text:
(type-name descriptor)
Return the descriptor's name qualified by its namespace, such as user/Point.

syntax-quote.text:
(syntax-quote template)
A quasiquote whose template names resolve where it is written. #`template reads as this form.
